problems.title: Normalized smooth spectra do not imply a common PAN factor
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v2, Appendix A.3, Proposition A.1 and Eqs.(31)–(39), PDF p.20; proceedings corresponding pp.19–20
claim: The PAN/intensity argument obtains \(I_{{\rm PAN},p}=I_p\int q(\lambda)C_p(\lambda)d\lambda\), then treats the integral as approximately spatially constant from normalized smooth chromaticity and a qualitative broadband response.
analysis: On \([0,1]\), take \(L=1,s=1-(1-a)\lambda\), spectra \(X_+=a\lambda^n,X_-=a(1-\lambda)^n\), and reflectances \(R_\pm=X_\pm/s\). For \(0<a<1\), these reflectances are smooth and in \([0,1]\), and both intensities are \(a/(n+1)\). Their factors are \[k_+=a+\frac{1-a}{n+2},\qquad k_-=1-\frac{1-a}{n+2}.\] With \(a=1/10,n=8\), they are \(19/100\) and \(91/100\); equal intensities produce PAN ratio \(91/19\). The best common positive calibration has worst relative intensity error \((k_--k_+)/(k_-+k_+)=36/55\).

The approximation has no stated tolerance, so a nonzero difference alone is not a refutation of a calibrated apparatus. The family demonstrates that no uniformly small error follows from the written qualitative premises. Flat response or common chromaticity rescues the factor; global image normalization cannot remove material-dependent differences. The valid scalar-illumination cancellation and known-intensity reconstruction algebra survive.
result: The physical-approximation justification needs quantitative calibration assumptions. This does not refute useful empirical PAN guidance or the known-intensity reconstruction method.
problems.impact_rationale: The supported defect limits a physical approximation argument, without a measured contradiction for the actual sensor or the central reconstruction results.
repair: The supplied bound is valid if \(\|q-k_0\|_\infty\leq\delta\) for known \(k_0>0\): \(|I_{\rm PAN}-k_0I|\leq\delta I\), hence relative calibrated error at most \(\delta/k_0\). A small actual ratio must be measured, not inferred from smoothness.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Dense top-k masking retains quadratic channel cost
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v2, Section 2.3 and Eq.(23); current author architecture/CIDNet.py, TopkOperation and Topk_WindowSpectralAttn
claim: The spectral-attention discussion attributes a reduction from \(O(C^2)\) to \(O(KC)\) to top-k masking, with fixed retained channel fractions.
analysis: The actual source first forms all \(d^2\) scores, then creates dense masks, dense softmax outputs and a dense value product for each of four fractions. With \(P\) window positions, this retains \(\Theta(Pd^2)\) work. Even ideal sparse aggregation with \(K=\lfloor\rho d\rfloor\), fixed \(\rho>0\), is \(\Theta(Pd^2)\). A valid \(O(KC)\) upper expression therefore does not establish a smaller asymptotic order here.
result: The mechanism sparsifies support; the inspected implementation does not establish the claimed resource reduction. No hardware timing or reconstruction score is contradicted by these analytic counts alone.
problems.impact_rationale: The resource interpretation needs a local correction, while learned reconstruction performance and measured end-to-end runtime are unrefuted.
repair: Retain dense quadratic cost for this implementation and distinguish it from any measured constant-factor benefit. No new sparse kernel is proposed.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Test reconstruction error controls checkpoint saving
problems.source_location: Latest arXiv v2 experimental protocol; current author train.py, test-data loading and epoch loop, lines 132–143
claim: The training driver evaluates the named test scenes each epoch, updates the maximum test PSNR, and saves improving checkpoints above its threshold.
analysis: The selected epoch depends on \(\arg\max_e\operatorname{PSNR}_{\rm test}(\theta_e)\). Thus test targets affect model selection even without entering gradient updates. This is separate from the explicitly declared intensity input. A score on the same selected test set is consequently not a wholly untouched holdout estimate under this driver.

The current release matches the implicated supplemental routine. The source alone does not establish which saved checkpoint generated each historical table, whether another final holdout existed, or the size of selection optimism.
result: The current selection protocol uses test error; empirical correction requires the actual checkpoint and evaluation history.
problems.impact_rationale: A concrete released selection path is established, but its attribution to published comparisons and numerical impact remains unresolved.
repair: Retain the supplied protocol correction: choose epochs using independent validation or a prespecified schedule, then evaluate on an untouched final test. No post hoc PSNR adjustment is justified.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.
